purpose: portfolio_concentration benchmark recalibration + Investment-domain-only re-test. Banking and Insurance untouched and not re-run. Validation only — no production artifact read or written, no Layer 3 rules defined.

step1_diagnosis.verdict: (a) the IDEAL was miscalibrated; the generator's marginal is the better-supported side and is left unchanged
evidence_for_generator: Goetzmann & Kumar (2008) Review of Finance 12(3):433-463, >40,000 discount-brokerage accounts 1991-96 — VERIFIED at source: retail investors are systematically under-diversified, more so when younger. The age gradient matches the generator's marginal taper (0.47 -> 0.25).
A largest-holding share near a third is the arithmetic consequence of holding few positions (max share >= 1/N, and real portfolios are not equal-weighted).

NOT VERIFIED AT SOURCE, flagged as such: secondary summaries reporting a mean of ~4 / median ~3 directly-held stocks (and Blume & Friend 1975 median 2). Consistent with the above but taken from summaries, not read in source.
scoring.py computes portfolio_concentration as max() over per-account concentration_risk, which overstates concentration — real values run at least as high as synthetic ones, never lower.

No SG-specific retail concentration statistic exists — re-confirmed absent across SGX market statistics, SIAS 2025 Retail Investor Pulse Survey, CDP materials and SingStat. This remains a judgement call.
evidence_against_old_ideal: Its sources (J.P. Morgan Private Bank 10-20%; Fidelity/Calamos/HDFC 5-10%) are PRESCRIPTIVE advisory thresholds for professionally-advised, largely high-net-worth clients — not descriptions of retail behaviour.
Unreachable at BOTH age extremes (3.7% of band 1, 3.8% of band 5 clear it), so the taper rate is not the defect — the level is.

step2_fix.citation_state: REASONED / STRUCTURAL, NOT CITED — same category as dti 0.15 and the net_worth ladder, not the same as LIA/MoneySense
step2_fix.rationale: <= 0.33 flat: largest holding at most a third of the portfolio, i.e. at least three meaningful positions. Reasoned/structural, NOT a cited benchmark — no SG retail concentration statistic exists (SGX/SIAS/CDP/SingStat re-checked). Direction corroborated by Goetzmann & Kumar 2008 (Review of Finance 12:433-463): retail investors are systematically under-diversified, more so when younger. Replaces the age-tapered 0.20-0.08 ladder, which came from PRESCRIPTIVE private-bank guidance (J.P. Morgan 10-20%, Fidelity/Calamos/HDFC 5-10%) and had a 4.2% population base rate.

rejected_alternatives.percentile_anchored: rejected — would import relative-to-sample ranking into a tier anchor, which the brief's Score Derivation constraint explicitly forbids
rejected_alternatives.regenerate_dataset: rejected — the generator is the better-supported side, and regenerating would invalidate the already-validated Banking and Insurance results
